summary: Round 1 (new module). The MARK is earned. `theoremA` is the conjunction of `theoremA_affine` (compact Hausdorff V with a locally projective structure of dimension n ⇒ V × S¹ locally affine of dimension n + 1) and `theoremA_projective` (p = q + 1 compact Hausdorff Vᵢ with locally projective structures of dimensions nᵢ ⇒ V₁ × … × V_p × S₁^{(p−1)} locally projective of dimension Σ nᵢ + q), each a one-line application of the two marked § 3 corollaries; compactness discharges their paracompact / σ-compact hypotheses through Mathlib instances, and the elaborated statements carry nothing else. The exponent is confirmed on the scan: journal p. 230 (PDF p. 3, rendered at 500 dpi) prints « V₁ × … × Vᵢ × … × V_p × S₁^{(p−1)} », roman S, subscript 1, parenthesised superscript p − 1 — the (p − 1)-fold power of the circle, as on p. 245 (three occurrences), and the only reading consistent with the dimension count (dim of the base of F(B₁) × … × F(B_p) = Σ dim Bᵢ + p − 1). Neither the labeled nor the orig transcription carries a flag at l.75 (the only comment in the block is « [sic] corrolaire »); the « guess » has no locus in the files, and the scan settles it. No issue beyond one nit for the ledger. Ready to graduate.

Printed A (p. 230, l.69–77): « Si une variété compacte V peut être munie d'une structure localement projective, le produit V × S₁ peut être muni d'une structure localement affine (S₁ désigne le cercle; cf. chap. 1, § 3, prop. 1, corrolaire). Si chacune des p variétés compactes Vᵢ peut être munie d'une structure localement projective, le produit V₁ × … × Vᵢ × … × V_p × S₁^{(p−1)} peut être muni d'une structure localement projective (chap. 1, § 3, prop. 3, corollaire). » Match: « variété compacte » = CompactSpace + T2Space (Hausdorff the « variété » reading; second countability automatic for a compact manifold, connectedness not needed — strictly more general), p ≥ 1 implicit in S₁^{(p−1)}, dimensions arbitrary per factor as printed, S₁ = Mathlib's Circle, the product V₁ × … × V_p as a Pi type over Fin p

Same notation on p. 245 (PDF p. 18): « topologiquement isomorphe à S₁^{(p−1)} », « B₁/G₁ × … × B_p/G_p × S₁^{(p−1)} », and the corollary. Meaning: the (p−1)-fold product of circles (the torus (ℝ^{+p}/ℝ^+)/H with H a lattice), which is the printed proof's construction and gives the right dimension Σ dim Bᵢ + p − 1. `Fin q → Circle` with p = q + 1 is that.
